claims.text: High local chemical disorder in (TaNb)HfZrTi induces local vibrational-mode softening.
Disorder-induced vibrational-mode softening enhances electron-phonon coupling in (TaNb)HfZrTi.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling increases Tc in (TaNb)HfZrTi.
Controlled annealing can produce partial chemical ordering in (TaNb)HfZrTi.
Partial chemical ordering reduces local vibrational anomalies.
Partial chemical ordering diminishes electron-phonon coupling and consequently lowers Tc.
The proposed mechanism requires disorder-induced pair-breaking scattering to remain a minor effect.
Rapid quenching preserves a highly or maximally chemically disordered state in this alloy.
Annealing at 750°C for 12 hours under inert atmosphere followed by quenching will induce partial chemical ordering.
EXAFS and atomic pair-distribution-function analysis can quantify local chemical order and atomic coordination environments.
Tunneling spectroscopy can be used to extract the electron-phonon coupling constant.
Transport measurements such as residual resistivity ratio can evaluate defect-induced scattering rates.
If the mechanism is correct, rapidly quenched samples will have a higher Tc than partially ordered annealed samples.
If the mechanism is correct, rapidly quenched samples will have a larger electron-phonon coupling constant than partially ordered annealed samples.
The mechanism is expected to apply only while compositional segregation and full phase separation are avoided.
The mechanism may fail when pair-breaking scattering dominates at extremely high disorder.
Secondary-phase formation or substantial compositional gradients would place the annealed comparison outside the proposed boundary conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the disordered samples do not exhibit both higher Tc and enhanced electron-phonon coupling relative to the annealed samples.
The hypothesis is also falsified if Tc differences track pair-breaking scattering more closely than electron-phonon coupling.
